subject: Urgent: Renewal support request — Anthem Data
messages:
From: Cora Hale <cora@anthemdata.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 15:07:00 -0500
Subject: Renewal negotiation — urgent request after incident

David —

Thanks again for the time last week. Anthem’s board is asking us to tighten budget ahead of year-end and they’ve flagged two things: the October outage on inference pipelines (our incident report attached) and the pricing delta compared to other vendors. Our renewal is due 11/30 and headcount + budget planning requires clarity this week.

We’re requesting the following as a condition for a two-year renewal:
- One-time service credit equal to 20% of our annual committed spend (to account for October incident impact)
- Reset of billing term to start on signing (move renewal anniversary by 3 months)
- SLA enhancement: include explicit availability credit clause (4 nines target with 5-day remedial window)

I realize this is outside standard terms. Can you escalate for exec approval? If we can get a conditional sign-off (subject to legal redlines) this week, procurement will proceed.

Attaching: incident report and a preliminary budget note.

– Cora
Head of Procurement, Anthem Data

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Cora Hale <cora@anthemdata.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Renewal negotiation — urgent request after incident

Hannah / Marcus —

Looping you both in. Anthem is a strategic mid-market account (RWI-2897). They experienced a two-hour regression Oct 28 that materially impacted a paid feature in production; incident report attached. Cora is asking for a one-time 20% credit, a 3-month term reset, and a bespoke SLA credit clause for the renewed agreement.

My read: account has strong usage but price sensitivity. We risk losing a ~$420k ARR renewal if we don’t offer meaningful concessions. Recommend we consider a bridge offer: 10% first-year credit + 30% committed discount for year 1 if they commit to 24 months, with a written SLA addendum that preserves our current SLOs but adds a clear credit schedule for major incidents. Legal will need to scope SLA language.

Can you advise authority and appetite for that structure? If approved, I’ll draft the proposed amendment and a conditional commercial memo for legal/finance.

Thanks — David
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts

--- Forwarded message attached (Anthem_Retention_Package_v2.pdf, service_incident_report_2026-10-28.pdf)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:32:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Fwd: Renewal negotiation — urgent request after incident

Marcus / David —

Thanks for the context. I’ve reviewed the incident report and Anthem’s ARR profile. Quick summary and recommendation below:

Summary:
- Renewal: ~ $420k ARR; renewal date 2026-11-30
- October incident caused measurable revenue impact for the customer
- Customer is open to 24-month term but requests both immediate financial remediation and stronger SLA language

Recommendation (commercially balanced):
1) One-time credit equal to 12% of committed ARR applied on invoice after signature (not retroactive beyond the current invoice cycle).
2) Year 1 list-price discount: 20% off published rates if they sign 24 months. Year 2 reverts to standard Tiers unless we negotiate renewal.
3) Term reset: move renewal date by 90 days to give procurement runway, subject to signature by 11/15.
4) SLA addendum: legal to accept a clarified availability credit schedule with a cap (3% annual credit cap) and a defined MTTR playbook — non-negotiable on unlimited exposure.

Conditions:
- Offer is conditional on Anthem signing a 24-month commitment and accepting limited legal redline on liability (no new indemnities).
- Offer expires EOD 11/12 to create urgency.

I can approve up to 15% one-time credit. To reach 20% or higher we need Marcus or an exec-level sign-off. If Marcus agrees with the framework, please confirm and I’ll instruct legal to prepare the amendment and CS to prepare an SLA appendix.

Hannah Schmitt
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Fwd: Renewal negotiation — urgent request after incident

Hannah / David —

Appreciate the crisp ask and the risk framing. Anthem is important given their product integrations and likelihood to expand into additional workloads next year. I’m willing to authorize the commercial structure with one change to increase chance of close:

- Increase one-time credit to 18% of ARR (from Hannah’s 12%) as a one-time concession, conditional on a firm 24-month term and a signed commercial memo by 11/12.
- Keep year 1 price discount at 20% as proposed.
- Term reset to start on signature is fine.
- SLA addendum: legal to draft with strict caps; no unlimited liability.

I need a short commercial justification memo (1 page) for finance and a clear churn risk note for our board. David — please prepare the memo and share the proposed amendment (redlines) in HubSpot and ping legal. Once I see the memo, I’ll give final sign-off and notify legal to proceed to redlines.

Marcus Lin
Head of Sales — East
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Cora Hale <cora@anthemdata.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Renewal negotiation — urgent request after incident

Cora / David —

Good news: Marcus has provisionally approved an elevated one-time concession of 18% of ARR in exchange for a firm 24-month commitment and signature by 11/12. Our next steps:

1) David: please upload the one-page commercial justification to HubSpot (HS-54321) and attach the redlined amendment (proposed_amendment_redlines.docx).
2) Legal: please draft the SLA addendum per the constraints above (3% annual credit cap, defined MTTR playbook) and circulate to Anthem procurement.
3) Commercial terms are conditional on Anthem signing the amendment and agreeing to limited liability language; once signed we will apply the 18% one-time credit on the first post-signature invoice and implement the term reset.

Cora — appreciate the patience. If you can confirm acceptance of these conditions by EOD 11/12 we’ll route the documents for signature immediately. If Anthem needs a slightly later window, let us know and we can triage internally.

Thanks all — Hannah
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
